post.originalText:
Claude Fable 5.2 vs Gemini 4 Carbon, same prompt: build a visually impressive 2.5D Snake game in one HTML file, but plan first so it burns as little of the usage limit as possible.

My take: Carbon's game looks and feels significantly better. Fable was faster. Numbers below.

Both ran on High. Before writing any code, each had to plan how to get the job done with minimal usage, so this tests efficiency as much as output.

Claude Fable 5.2 ($100 plan)
• 22 min
• 8% of the 5-hour limit
• 1% of the weekly limit, 2% of the Fable weekly limit

Gemini 4 Carbon (Google AI Ultra, $200 plan)
• 34 min
• 1% of the 5-hour limit
• 0-1% of the weekly limit

Gameplay from both is in the video.

Coming soon: this "plan first to save tokens" approach vs a standard build, to see what the planning step actually changes.

sourceMaterials.text: @shipwithstef Thank you Stef! And actually it allowed Carbon to actually do the damn job 😅 Because now I'm trying to see how much time & limits the same task will take without planning it to take less tokens and guess what... Fable 5.2 used out way more limits & took ~45 minutes, meanwhile... Carbon is still in it's initial thinking phase, I feel like it's going to just crash once again after an hour of thinking... 😂
